research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is Executive Order 5825 of March 26, 1932, Leaves of Absence, Foreign Service, held as the official compilation Proclamations and Executive Orders: Herbert Hoover, vol. II (OFR/GPO 1974), printed page 1115, PDF page 344 (OCR text layer of the scan, grade official_compilation_high; the order predates the Federal Register). The census register row (1932-03-26, Herbert Hoover) and the WPA 1944 list entry for March 26, 1932 (page 501, amending the Instructions to Diplomatic Officers and the Consular Regulations on leave without compensation) agree. The page identification comes from the held text's own header; I did not view the page image. I read the whole held text: one enacting sentence amending paragraph (d) of section 8, chapter VI, of the Instructions to Diplomatic Officers and paragraph (d) of section 467 of the Consular Regulations of 1896, and the new paragraph (d), Leave without compensation. The dossier's two scopes (lead, d) cover it; I confirm the inventory. Ending: Executive Order 8189 of July 5, 1939 (4 FR 2783, Federal Register of July 7, 1939) lists this order under the heading 'Revocation of Executive Orders'. The same order cancels listed provisions of the Foreign Service Regulations and adds a new section on leaves of absence, so the revocation comes with a replacement. EO 8189 has no delayed-effect wording; the sentences 'This order shall become effective on July 1, 1939' on the same Federal Register page belong to the orders that follow its signature block, EOs 8190 and 8191. The end is therefore its signing date, July 5, 1939 (its filing on July 6 and publication on July 7, 1939 are the alternative readings). Machine searches reported no hits for the number 5825, so the revocation comes from the by-number search of held texts and my reading of EO 8189. No earlier end: I read the held orders of 1932-1939 amending the Instructions to Diplomatic Officers or the Consular Regulations (EOs 6737, 6810, 7012, 7013, 7261, 7449); none touches leave of absence. The order was not operative on 2026-10-14; provisional status NO is unchanged. The text rests on an OCR layer of an official compilation, not a human transcription.

savings.reason: EO 8189 revokes EO 5825 without exception or saving: its revocation list is unqualified and no provision of EO 8189 preserves paragraph (d). Leave of absence is afterwards governed by the new section and regulations the Secretary of State prescribes, a replacement and not a continuation of EO 5825. Nothing held shows rights or acts accrued under EO 5825 that were saved.
